name: Antonian movement (Kimpa Vita)

dating.dating_summary: A dated, bounded reform movement: began 1704 with Kimpa Vita's claimed possession by Saint Anthony of Padua; ended with her execution by burning in 1706.

earliest_written_attestation.note: No surviving African-authored primary source exists; the entire documentary record consists of accounts by Italian Capuchin missionaries (chiefly Bernardo da Gallo and Lorenzo da Lucca), hostile witnesses given she was tried and executed as a heretic largely on their testimony.

tradition_internal_claim.note: Kimpa Vita claimed to have died and been reincarnated/possessed by Saint Anthony of Padua in 1704, and preached that Jesus, Mary, and the saints were themselves Kongolese/African.

notes: John K. Thornton, The Kongolese Saint Anthony: Dona Beatriz Kimpa Vita and the Antonian Movement, 1684-1706 (Cambridge UP, 1998) — the foundational modern academic monograph, reading the hostile Capuchin sources "against the grain." Movement arose amid civil wars over the Kongo throne following the 1665 Battle of Mbwila; Thornton frames it as having taken on the character of "something of a theocracy," aimed at ending the wars and restoring unified sacralized kingship. Executed on orders connected to King Pedro IV, with Capuchin missionary involvement in her heresy condemnation. See claim_kimpa_vita_does_not_demonstrate.
